clue.text: Second inside right to succeed

indicators.note: inside says the first item sits within the word that follows it

parts.note: proper means right or correct
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A runner-up stepping into the right-hand seat to take over from a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes into the middle of PROPER to make PROSPER.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to do well or flourish, a close synonym of succeed.

clue.text: Old man outside with gold box opener

indicators.note: being outside means wrapping around the rest

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, an old man
and means with or plus
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An elderly man handing over a box containing gold.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Pandora opened the jar, later called a box, that released evils into the world.

clue.text: Circle line's moving apart from Northern in bounds of Bank/Monument

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters between the outer pair
moving letters around rearranges them
apart from means excluding, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
line with its s
N is the abbreviation for Northern

indicators.note: the bounds of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of Bank

explanation.surface: A London Underground announcement: the Circle line is running, but not the Northern, between Bank and Monument stations.
explanation.walkthrough: Circle, Northern, Bank and Monument are all London Underground names, which makes the clue read like a travel bulletin; only Monument is a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall tapering stone pillar erected as a monument or memorial.

clue.text: Rhythm's winning over university

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead, winning
LSE is the London School of Economics, a university

explanation.surface: A beat that wins over a university audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winning over' reads as persuading someone, but over is the signal to turn the first piece around. LSE is the London School of Economics.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is a regular beat or throb, which is a rhythm in music or the body.

clue.text: X-ray image reflected Mrs Leadbetter — I had a right!

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the whole string runs backwards

parts.note: Margo Leadbetter is the snobbish neighbour in the British sitcom The Good Life
I'd is the contraction of I had
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Margo Leadbetter boasting that she was entitled to an X-ray.
explanation.walkthrough: MARGO ID A R read backwards gives the answer. The Good Life was a 1970s BBC comedy about self-sufficiency in suburbia.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiogram is a photographic image made by X-rays or other radiation, also called a radiograph.

clue.text: Ministers start to talk, after church, about a case

indicators.note: after places this letter behind the group built from the church
about means going around something, so the church abbreviation wraps the following words

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
taken as written
a bin is a container or case for storing things

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: opening letter of talk

explanation.surface: Government ministers beginning a discussion after a church service about some legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: The commas split the clue into a two-step build: the church wraps 'a case', and only then does the start of talk go on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabinet is the body of senior government ministers who decide policy together.

clue.text: Angry about Rachel's choice?

parts.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
in the sitcom Friends, Rachel ends up choosing Ross

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether Rachel's decision was made in anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cross means being annoyed or irritated, a mild synonym of angry.

clue.text: National British bird adopted by rising international alliance

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so it sits inside
in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization
a swan is a bird

explanation.surface: A British bird taken into care by an ascendant international alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Botswanan is a citizen of Botswana, a national of that southern African country.

clue.text: Did career upset deserve recount?

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, which in a down clue reverses the word

parts.note: to career is to rush, so did career means ran
to rate is to merit or deserve

explanation.surface: A disappointed candidate wondering whether a botched job earned a recount of votes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recount' suggests a vote recount, but here it means to tell. RAN runs upward to NAR, then RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount is to tell a story or relate events, the same as narrate.

clue.text: Artist with full set of awards keeping quiet about TV show

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the whole string runs backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the next item goes inside

parts.note: an EGOT is winning all four of an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar and Tony
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: An artist who has won every award keeps quiet about a television programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The quiet letter goes in after the second letter of the award set, and the whole string is then read backwards. Top Gear is a BBC motoring programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Gear is a long-running British television show about cars and motoring.

clue.text: Exasperated call for light

parts.note: to call for something is to need it
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small light

explanation.surface: Someone irritated and demanding that a lamp be switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: To be needled is to be irritated or provoked, as though pricked repeatedly.

clue.text: Cut more than rock?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... someone is to crop or trim more than they do, read as OUT plus CROP
second meaning: a mass of bedrock showing above the ground surface

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is an invented verb, the out- prefix meaning surpass as in outrun, attached to crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists call an exposed piece of bedrock that protrudes from the soil an outcrop.

clue.text: Aromatic duck eaten by certain dog on the counter

indicators.note: counter suggests running against the normal direction, so the words are read backwards
something eaten ends up inside whatever consumes it

parts.note: sure means certain
Fido is a stock name for a dog
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A smelly duck being gobbled by a dog on a kitchen worktop.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'counter' looks like a kitchen worktop but signals reading backwards; the duck goes in after that reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Odiferous, a variant of odoriferous, means giving off a smell, so an aromatic substance qualifies.

clue.text: Perhaps Willy Wonka's beginning well

indicators.note: a word's beginning is just its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of Wonka
hale means healthy or well

explanation.surface: Willy Wonka, the chocolate factory owner, is in good health at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Willy looks like Willy Wonka, but it is the definition by example: the orca in the film Free Willy. The clue's 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy, star of the film Free Willy, is an orca, a type of toothed whale, so the clue's 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: An artist's unfinished joint

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
Paul Klee was a Swiss-German painter

explanation.surface: A painter's half-finished picture of a joint of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: KLEE loses its last letter to give KLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge connecting foot and leg, a joint of the body.

clue.text: Cheese and ham melt cooked around middle of tent

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the selected letters go inside
cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters

parts.note: middle two letters of tent

explanation.surface: A toasted ham-and-cheese melt cooked over a campfire beside a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmenthal is a Swiss cheese with large holes, named after the Emme valley.

clue.text: Storyteller wholly avoiding nuclear reactor after explosion

indicators.note: an explosion scatters things, so the letters are blown into a new order
avoiding means keeping clear of, so those letters are left out

parts.note: taken as written
clear can mean completely, as in jumping clear over a fence

explanation.surface: A survivor of a reactor blast tells the tale, having kept well away from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The fourteen letters of NUCLEAR REACTOR rearrange to include CLEAR; removing those five leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a person skilled at telling anecdotes and stories entertainingly.

clue.text: One of 21 in agreement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a letter other than a vowel, of which the alphabet has twenty-one
second meaning: harmonious or consistent with

explanation.walkthrough: 21 looks like a cross-reference to 21 Down, but it is just a number: English has 21 letters that are not vowels.
explanation.definitionFit: Consonant also means in harmony, as in 'consonant with the evidence', describing things that agree.

clue.text: FBI agent arresting board with tip from spiteful union aide

indicators.note: arresting someone means holding them, so the agent wraps around what follows

parts.note: a G-man is American slang for an FBI agent
to board with someone is to room or lodge with them

indicators.note: a word's tip is one of its ends, here its first letter

parts.note: first letter of spiteful

explanation.surface: An FBI agent apprehends a malicious trade union official with help from a tip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union aide' looks like a trade union official; the union is a marriage. G-MAN holds ROOM plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: A groomsman is a friend who helps the bridegroom at a wedding, the union of a couple.

clue.text: FA messed with digit for tax scheme

indicators.note: messing with letters jumbles them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Football Association tampering with a figure to dodge a tax arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA is England's Football Association; Gift Aid lets UK charities reclaim basic-rate tax on donations.
explanation.definitionFit: Gift Aid is the UK government arrangement letting charities claim back income tax on gifts.

clue.text: Like some illusions, best when using the other extreme of magic

indicators.text: when using the other extreme of
indicators.note: using the other extreme means swapping one end letter of a word for the opposite end

parts.note: optimal means best
the far end of magic, replacing its first letter

explanation.surface: A magician's best illusion depends on the end of the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: OPTIMAL holds the M of magic; swap it for the other end of magic, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical illusions are tricks of sight, so optical describes some kinds of illusion.

clue.text: New king possibly ceding crown for Beatrice or Eugenie?

indicators.note: giving up the crown means losing the top, the first letter

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
a king is one example of a chess piece

explanation.surface: A new king perhaps giving up the throne in favour of one of the young princesses.
explanation.walkthrough: PIECE loses its first letter to give IECE. The royal surface makes 'king' look literal, but it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Princesses Beatrice and Eugenie are daughters of Prince Andrew, so they are nieces of King Charles III.

clue.text: Summing up of transcendental numbers needing book

parts.note: e and pi are the two best-known transcendental numbers
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A mathematical summary of transcendental numbers calling for a textbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summing up' looks like arithmetic, but it means a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a brief summary of a larger work, as well as a perfect example.

clue.text: Complex character edited Lear etc

indicators.note: editing reworks text, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complicated character from King Lear and other plays, revised by an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex character' sounds like a complicated personality, but it is the figure who names the Electra complex.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra, Agamemnon's daughter in Greek tragedy, gives her name to Jung's Electra complex.

clue.text: Pleasure to take to bed

indicators.note: to take something is to hold it, so the first word encloses the next

parts.note: fun is pleasure or enjoyment
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suggestive invitation to retire for some pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take to bed' looks like a phrase, but take is the containment signal and bed alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style padded mattress used as a bed, often on a low frame.

clue.text: With what an isosceles triangle might have?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: together with or beside

definitions.text: what an isosceles triangle might have?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as three words: an isosceles triangle may have two short equal sides and one long one

explanation.walkthrough: The geometric reading splits the answer into A LONG SIDE; the question mark flags this whimsical split.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside works as a preposition meaning together with or in company with, the same as with.

clue.text: Everyone — I see God!

parts.note: all means everyone
ah is an exclamation of understanding, like I see

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming that they have had a vision of the divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Allah is the Arabic name for God, used in Islam.

clue.text: Manager missing final own goal

indicators.note: missing its final letter means the end is cut off

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss, especially a football manager

explanation.surface: A football manager despairing over an own goal in the last match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing final' sounds like missing a cup final, but it removes the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An own goal figuratively means a self-inflicted blunder, and a gaffe is an embarrassing mistake.

clue.text: Beer, briefly chilled, containing hot sauce

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the next item goes within
a word said briefly is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
cool means chilled
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A chilled beer served with a spicy hot sauce on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot sauce' reads like a condiment, but sauce is the definition: slang for alcoholic drink, as in 'on the sauce'. AL then COOL holding H.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is informal slang for liquor, as in someone being on the sauce, meaning drinking heavily.

clue.text: Slight female seen in hairstyle books

indicators.note: seen in places one item within the other

parts.note: an Afro is a rounded hairstyle of tight curls
F is the abbreviation for female
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A slender woman spotted in a salon's catalogue of hairstyles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective for the woman, but it is a noun meaning insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub or insult, and an affront is a deliberate act of disrespect.

clue.text: Temptress from US city visiting New Delhi

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside the place visited
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the city's letters

parts.note: taken as written
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A seductive woman from Los Angeles on a trip to India's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Delhi' reads as the city's full name, but New is the anagram signal for DELHI alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Delilah, who betrayed Samson in the Bible, has become a byword for a seductive, treacherous woman.

clue.text: Counting seven from August, here's April and May?

indicators.note: counting off seven letters from a point means taking a run of consecutive letters out of the words

parts.note: seven letters running from the end of the first word into the third

explanation.surface: Counting months on a calendar from August, with April and May coming up.
explanation.walkthrough: The months make it look like a calendar puzzle, but May is the former British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa May was UK Prime Minister from 2016 to 2019, so May with a question mark hints at her first name.
